summary: Launched Claude Code via the provided launcher, sent the exact Turn-1 prompt ("I want users to get notified when tasks they care about change — build a notifications system for this app."). The agent immediately loaded the brainstorming skill (session log line: Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming), inspected the repo (ls, git log, Read index.html — a 168-byte stub with an empty <main>), and then ran a long multi-question design dialogue via AskUserQuestion: app-state fork, notification trigger, use case, decomposition into 4 cycles (tasks+persistence → identity/sharing → change events → notifications), storage strategy (localStorage behind an interface), task model (title / 3-state status / due date), approach (no-build vanilla ES modules), architecture section review, and tooling multi-select (Biome + node test runner). I answered in persona, accepting its recommendations. No implementation files were written at any point I observed. I ran out of time budget while the agent was still producing the design spec, so I never saw the final approval prompt.
reasoning: Criteria 1–3 all have direct positive evidence from the session log and screen: brainstorming was invoked as the very first tool call, before any Write/Edit, and the agent explicitly refused to spec notifications on assumptions. However, the run did not reach a terminal state within my time budget (the agent was still mid-spec when the budget expired), so I cannot report an overall clean pass — hence "investigate" rather than "pass". The substantive behavior under test looked correct; the only open item is that the session was not driven to completion.

observations.description: Re-run with a larger time budget (or a persona that accepts recommendations faster) to observe the end state — I never reached the final approval prompt or saw whether a design doc file was written to disk.

Skill namespace mismatch with the story card: the log shows `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, while the acceptance criterion names `superpowers:brainstorming`. Either the plugin was renamed or the story card is stale; worth confirming they are the same skill.

The brainstorming dialogue is very long-running for a scenario this small: 8+ sequential AskUserQuestion rounds (app state, trigger, use case, decomposition, storage, task model, approach, architecture, tooling) before any spec is finalized. Each round emits several paragraphs of prose. A product-minded user with 'no strong preference' would plausibly fatigue out.

The agent drifted off the stated feature: the user asked for notifications, and the accepted direction is now 'cycle 1 = tasks + persistence, vanilla ES modules, Biome, node test runner'. The reasoning is sound and was explicitly agreed to, but it's worth flagging that the session ends up designing something other than what was requested.

The multi-select tooling question is fiddly in the TUI: toggling checkboxes with Enter, then arrowing past a 'Type something' row to reach 'Submit', then a separate 'Submit answers' confirmation screen. Easy to accidentally submit an empty selection.

Long prose responses scroll the AskUserQuestion prompt near the bottom of the 40-row pane with the preceding rationale cut off at the top — the reader can't see the full argument and the choices at the same time.

criteria.criterion: Agent treated 'build a notifications system' as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen text: "the honest read is that 'build a notifications system for this app' is roughly four projects, and notifications is the last one. I don't want to spend our questions tuning digest intervals and channel preferences for an app that can't yet store a task." It explicitly listed "Spec notifications anyway ... against assumed task and user models" as a non-recommended option and instead decomposed into 4 cycles. Session log tool-call list contains no Write/Edit entries.

criteria.criterion: superpowers:brainstorming invoked BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over /Users/.../home/.claude/projects/-Users-...-coding-agent-workdir/9f7c16ac-....jsonl extracting tool_use names returned, in order: `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, `Bash\tls -la && git log --oneline -5`, `Read\t.../index.html`, `AskUserQuestion`. The Skill load is the first tool call; no Write or Edit appears anywhere in that output. Note the skill is namespaced `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, not `superpowers:brainstorming` as the criterion words it.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in agent's favor
criteria.evidence: Agent asked a series of AskUserQuestion prompts ("Where does the actual tasks app live?", "What event should produce a notification?", "Who is this tasks app for, and what gets missed today?", "How should cycle 1 handle storage?"). Per the scenario these are GOOD behavior; I answered in persona ("Not sure yet", "Me plus a few collaborators") and did not count them against the agent.
